chapters.text: CHAPTER 17 · ENGINEERING KNOWLEDGE AI, RAG & Tool Security Version Reviewed Architecture scope 2.0.0 2 November 2026 Keep retrieved content and model output outside the trusted policy boundary. 1. Description, Purpose and Boundaries Keep retrieved content and model output outside the trusted policy boundary. Separate trusted policy and tool permissions from retrieved documents, email bodies and model output. Treat ai, rag & tool security as an independently reviewable capability. Trace its inputs, processing decisions and acceptance evidence before applying it to a live system. The examples define bounded units; external services need separately verified permissions, contracts and environment configuration. 2. Architectural Principles and Decisions The primary decision boundary is: Generate with scoped context and approved tools. Application logic and an accountable owner establish this decision. Preserve the input identity and rule revision so its outcome can be investigated. Prioritize retrieved document injects tool instructions and deleted data remains in embeddings. Establish checks for these failures before enabling automation. Completion requires evidence for the final step, validate citations, arguments and budget before action, rather than merely observing request acceptance. 3. Process, Inputs and Outputs Step Action Evidence 1 Filter knowledge by authorized tenant and provenance Approved input scope, source and owner 2 Generate with scoped context and approved tools Recorded decision, revision and exception handling 3 Validate citations, arguments and budget before action Observed outcome and recovery or rollback decision Stop at any boundary whose required evidence cannot be established. If an external side effect may already have occurred, reconcile its durable identity before retrying. 4. Related Apps, Software and Third Parties Component Role Integration responsibility Vector index Evidence retrieval Verify supported contract, least privilege, account access, data handling, quotas and ownership. Model API Generation Verify supported contract, least privilege, account access, data handling, quotas and ownership. Scoped tool gateway Permission enforcement Verify supported contract, least privilege, account access, data handling, quotas and ownership. These products are candidates for this capability, not a claim that they are connected to this documentation site. Choose them by boundary responsibility and measured requirements. Keep their private credentials outside public HTML. 5. Detailed Mechanics and Topic Features Knowledge pipeline Collect approved sources, record provenance and access permissions, parse and chunk documents, create embeddings and index them. At retrieval time filter by tenant/authorization before sending context to a model. Include source references and allow unknown answers. Plan reindexing and deletion so removed private data does not remain retrievable. Agents and tools Give each tool a narrow schema and least-privilege credential. Validate arguments outside the model, enforce budgets and require the project’s approval gates for consequential actions. Retrieved instructions must not override system policy. Treat prompt injection as an ongoing threat; a prompt disclaimer alone is not a control. Evaluation and memory Use a held-out dataset for groundedness, task accuracy, injection resistance, privacy leakage, tool misuse, latency and cost. Store only necessary user-approved memory with retention and deletion controls. Avoid raw secrets and sensitive identifiers in prompts, embeddings and traces. Log tool decisions and redacted outcomes rather than hidden reasoning. Deployment decisions Compare quality, data-processing terms, region, latency and cost using verified current provider information. Treat the legacy playbook’s model names, prices, improvement percentages and autonomy thresholds as examples, not production guarantees. 6. Implementation Pattern and Copyable Code This focused TypeScript implementation belongs in the trusted application or test layer. Supply identity, permission and provider-verification state from real verified dependencies; do not accept trust flags directly from a browser. typescript Copy code interface Evidence { id: string; tenantId: string; authorized: boolean; content: string; } export function buildEvidenceContext( tenantId: string, records: readonly Evidence[] ): string { return records .filter(record => record.tenantId === tenantId && record.authorized) .map(record => JSON.stringify({ sourceId: record.id, untrustedDocumentText: record.content })) .join("\n"); } // Authorization must be established by trusted retrieval logic. // JSON encoding does not neutralize prompt injection on its own. Version the implementation with the consuming application and run this chapter’s acceptance checks when its assumptions change. A copied unit does not establish that all external integrations are active. 7. Failure Modes, Edge Cases and Security Failure Containment Retrieved document injects tool instructions Stop the affected operation; inspect its last durable boundary and redacted evidence. Reconcile uncertain side effects before retrying and add a regression case. Deleted data remains in embeddings Stop the affected operation; inspect its last durable boundary and redacted evidence. Reconcile uncertain side effects before retrying and add a regression case. Authorize tenant-owned inputs and artifacts explicitly. Distinguish permanent validation failures from transient dependency errors. Exclude raw session tokens, credentials, OTPs and private content from routine logs. 9. Acceptance, Testing and Verification Matrix Case Expected outcome Evidence Unauthorized documents are never retrieved Condition holds in the intended environment; failure blocks approval. Tested revision, input, observed result and reviewer Proposed tools cannot exceed caller permissions Condition holds in the intended environment; failure blocks approval. Record the dependency contract, environment and last tested revision. Use the failure matrix to locate uncertain state during incidents. Preserve redacted evidence, restore the approved configuration or apply a reviewed correction, and rerun acceptance checks. Update the review date after provider or architectural changes. 11. chapters.text: CHAPTER 14 · ENGINEERING KNOWLEDGE APIs, Webhooks & Integrations Version Reviewed Architecture scope 2.0.0 2 November 2026 Keep integrations bounded, authenticated and replay-safe. 1. Description, Purpose and Boundaries Keep integrations bounded, authenticated and replay-safe. Define contracts and failure handling before connecting external systems. Treat apis, webhooks & integrations as an independently reviewable capability. Trace its inputs, processing decisions and acceptance evidence before applying it to a live system. The examples define bounded units; external services need separately verified permissions, contracts and environment configuration. 2. Architectural Principles and Decisions The primary decision boundary is: Execute idempotent authorized operation. Application logic and an accountable owner establish this decision. Preserve the input identity and rule revision so its outcome can be investigated. Prioritize webhook signature checked after modifying payload and retry duplicates a side effect. Establish checks for these failures before enabling automation. Completion requires evidence for the final step, persist result and acknowledge with correlation id, rather than merely observing request acceptance. 3. Process, Inputs and Outputs Step Action Evidence 1 Validate caller, schema and payload size Approved input scope, source and owner 2 Execute idempotent authorized operation Recorded decision, revision and exception handling 3 Persist result and acknowledge with correlation ID Observed outcome and recovery or rollback decision Stop at any boundary whose required evidence cannot be established. If an external side effect may already have occurred, reconcile its durable identity before retrying. 4. Related Apps, Software and Third Parties Component Role Integration responsibility HTTP gateway Request validation Verify supported contract, least privilege, account access, data handling, quotas and ownership. Provider webhook External event input Verify supported contract, least privilege, account access, data handling, quotas and ownership. Queue Deferred event processing Verify supported contract, least privilege, account access, data handling, quotas and ownership. These products are candidates for this capability, not a claim that they are connected to this documentation site. Choose them by boundary responsibility and measured requirements. Keep their private credentials outside public HTML. 5. Detailed Mechanics and Topic Features API design Use explicit request/response schemas, server-side validation, pagination, bounded payload sizes and consistent errors. Authenticate callers and authorize each resource. Add request IDs and per-principal rate limits. Use idempotency keys for retryable mutations and persist the outcome atomically with the operation. Never trust client-reported payment or identity-verification success. Webhooks Verify the provider signature against the raw payload using its documented algorithm and freshness checks. Reject unauthenticated events, deduplicate event IDs, persist receipt and acknowledge promptly before asynchronous processing. Support out-of-order delivery and retries with a state machine. Keep replay tooling and a dead-letter queue. A public endpoint and a secret URL alone are insufficient verification. External calls and files Set timeouts, bounded retries, circuit breakers and cancellation. Apply SSRF controls to user-provided URLs. Validate upload size, content and ownership; scan where appropriate and use short-lived download grants. Store attachments in object storage with tenant-aware access. Treat all third-party content as untrusted data. Contract checks Exercise malformed payloads, missing fields, oversized input, bad signatures, duplicated events, timeout-after-success, dependency outage and rate-limit responses. Document versioning, deprecation and incident ownership. 6. Implementation Pattern and Copyable Code This focused TypeScript implementation belongs in the trusted application or test layer. Version the implementation with the consuming application and run this chapter’s acceptance checks when its assumptions change. A copied unit does not establish that all external integrations are active. 7. chapters.text: CHAPTER 10 · ENGINEERING KNOWLEDGE Authentication & SSO Version Reviewed Architecture scope 2.0.0 2 November 2026 Prove identity using a verified provider or application-owned sign-in flow. 1. Description, Purpose and Boundaries Prove identity using a verified provider or application-owned sign-in flow. Authentication proves identity; authorization decides what that identity can do. Keep the two responsibilities explicit. Treat authentication & sso as an independently reviewable capability. Trace its inputs, processing decisions and acceptance evidence before applying it to a live system. The examples define bounded units; external services need separately verified permissions, contracts and environment configuration. 2. Architectural Principles and Decisions The primary decision boundary is: Resolve verified identity to active membership. Application logic and an accountable owner establish this decision. Preserve the input identity and rule revision so its outcome can be investigated. Prioritize account linking trusts unverified email and recovery bypasses the primary factor. Establish checks for these failures before enabling automation. Completion requires evidence for the final step, create a session at the required assurance level, rather than merely observing request acceptance. 3. If an external side effect may already have occurred, reconcile its durable identity before retrying. 4. WebAuthn Passkey authentication Verify supported contract, least privilege, account access, data handling, quotas and ownership. OIDC provider Federated identity Verify supported contract, least privilege, account access, data handling, quotas and ownership. These products are candidates for this capability, not a claim that they are connected to this documentation site. Choose them by boundary responsibility and measured requirements. Keep their private credentials outside public HTML. 5. Detailed Mechanics and Topic Features Methods and tradeoffs Passwords require secure password hashing, recovery and abuse controls. Email OTP proves current access to a mailbox and is not phishing-resistant. Magic links are bearer credentials that can leak through forwarded messages. TOTP uses authenticator-generated time codes; recovery codes need protected storage and one-time consumption. Passkeys use WebAuthn and origin binding. OIDC provides federated sign-in; OAuth alone is delegated authorization. SAML supports enterprise federation. Role-specific policy Create an explicit policy matrix for administrator, user, employee, client, applicant and demo roles. For the user’s projects that specify Duo-only administration, enforce the Duo SSO flow server-side and do not expose an alternative route that bypasses it. Other projects may have different approved policies; do not copy a single app’s policy globally. Employee application SSO and administrator Cloudflare Access protections are separate architectural decisions. Federated sign-in checklist Use supported identity-provider libraries. Validate issuer, audience, signature, expiry, state and nonce where applicable; use PKCE for authorization-code flows. Allowlist redirect URIs. Link accounts only after proving control of the identities; matching an unverified email is insufficient. Apply application roles after identity verification and fail closed if provider checks fail. Enrollment and recovery Require reauthentication for factor changes, email changes and account linking. Notify users of security changes. Protect recovery paths as strongly as sign-in and audit privileged recovery. Plan lost-device recovery, provider outage behavior, account suspension and session revocation. Test denied users, stale roles, invalid callbacks and blocked direct API requests. 6. Version the implementation with the consuming application and run this chapter’s acceptance checks when its assumptions change. Budget ledger Admission accounting Verify supported contract, least privilege, account access, data handling, quotas and ownership. Model adapter Transport boundary Verify supported contract, least privilege, account access, data handling, quotas and ownership. These products are candidates for this capability, not a claim that they are connected to this documentation site. Choose them by boundary responsibility and measured requirements. Keep their private credentials outside public HTML. 5. Detailed Architecture, Implementation and Tests Page 1 — Production AI Application Architecture and Request Lifecycle Metadata Value Document version 1.0.0 Last reviewed 2 November 2026 Target scope Tenant-aware, server-controlled AI inference service; TypeScript application core; GitHub CI; Cloudflare application hosting; managed model adapters Audience Platform engineers, application developers, security reviewers and operations owners Implementation boundary A complete, provider-independent request-lifecycle module and executable acceptance tests. Identity verification, durable accounting and provider transport are explicit service contracts. Release status Architecture reference. Production approval requires the verification matrix below to pass against the actual deployed dependencies. 1. Architectural overview and governing principles An AI application must control more than model invocation. It must determine who is asking, which tenant owns the request, whether the requested operation is permitted, which data may leave the system, how much work is affordable, and what happens if the client or provider fails halfway through processing. The model is an untrusted computational dependency. It does not establish identity, assign roles, choose unrestricted network destinations or authorize side effects. The application makes these decisions before invoking it and validates its result afterward. A model-generated string cannot change a permission policy. The request lifecycle below supports bounded text inference without tools. Tool execution, retrieval, email delivery and account enrollment are separate service capabilities. Their absence is deliberate: an inference endpoint must not accidentally acquire authority to send messages or mutate business records simply because a model supports function calling. 1.1 Trust boundaries flowchart TD U["Untrusted client"] --> G["Request gateway"] G --> I["Identity and tenant checks"] I --> A{"Admission policy"} A -->|Reject| R["Safe error"] A -->|Admit| B["Durable budget reservation"] B --> M["Scoped model adapter"] M --> V["Response validation"] V --> S["Accounting settlement"] S --> O["Response and redacted audit"] Mermaid source Copy Mermaid flowchart TD U["Untrusted client"] --> G["Request gateway"] G --> I["Identity and tenant checks"] I --> A{"Admission policy"} A -->|Reject| R["Safe error"] A -->|Admit| B["Durable budget reservation"] B --> M["Scoped model adapter"] M --> V["Response validation"] V --> S["Accounting settlement"] S --> O["Response and redacted audit"] The client boundary accepts only a task name, an input string and an output-token ceiling. Tenant membership and permissions arrive from authenticated server state. The adapter boundary translates the application contract into one provider's current API. Budget enforcement happens in a durable accounting boundary shared by all application instances. Each boundary has an independent failure policy. Authentication failure must not fall through to an anonymous paid request. Budget failure must not invoke the model. A provider timeout is an uncertain outcome because processing may continue remotely. A settlement failure must not silently discard the accounting obligation. 1.2 Non-negotiable invariants 1. Every admitted request has a verified principal with an active tenant membership. 2. Every model call follows a successful budget reservation. 3. The reservation precedes the side effect and includes a unique request identifier. 4. Provider selection comes from an approved server registry, never a client-supplied URL. 5. Unsupported tasks and token limits fail before provider invocation. 6. A timeout or transport failure retains its reservation until reconciliation establishes usage or releases it safely. 7. Prompts, API credentials, session tokens and generated private text are excluded from routine logs. 8. The provider's answer remains data. Rendering it must not execute HTML, scripts or commands. 2. Detailed system mechanics 2.1 Identity and authorization The HTTP authentication layer verifies the session or access token and constructs a Principal. The principal's user ID, tenant ID and permission set must come from the verified identity and membership records. A browser-submitted tenant header is merely a requested tenant and must be checked against membership. A permission check applies to the operation, not just the page. A user who can view the chat interface does not automatically have permission to invoke every model, export tenant knowledge or execute administrative tools. The reference module requires the ai:generate permission and an active membership. Permission changes introduce cache invalidation requirements. A suspended account must lose access within the defined revocation window. If membership is cached, document the maximum stale interval and bypass that cache for privileged actions. Tokens with tenant or role claims require server-side validation and a strategy for revocation. 2.2 Input boundaries and token accounting Limit HTTP body bytes before parsing JSON. After parsing, reject unknown properties, invalid types, blank inputs and unsupported tasks. A character limit is not a token estimate: UTF-8 byte length, Unicode code points and provider tokenization differ. The accounting service must reserve a conservative upper bound derived from the full provider request: developer instructions, user input, retrieved context, tool schemas, image/audio charges when applicable, the output ceiling and the provider's billing model. The reference uses reservation units rather than money to avoid pretending that a single universal price calculation fits every model. Provider usage is authoritative only after validating the response schema. Missing usage is an accounting uncertainty, not zero cost. For metered production systems, reconcile provider billing records against application reservations. 2.3 Registry and task routing A registry entry records the task, adapter key, approved model ID, token ceiling and data-processing policy. At deployment, validate each entry against the provider's current capability schema. A model supporting text input does not necessarily support a particular structured-output format, tool schema or reasoning parameter. As of this review, official catalogs list GPT-6 Astra, GPT-6.1 Sol, GPT-6.1 Terra and GPT-6 Luna; Claude Fable 5.1, Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5 and Haiku 5.5; and Gemini 4 Argon and Gemini 3.8 Flash. These are candidate families, not interchangeable endpoint contracts. Choose a model using representative task evaluations and verify account availability. The code below intentionally does not hardcode a provider or a model alias. 2.4 Budget lifecycle and uncertain completion stateDiagram-v2 [*] --> Reserved: atomic admission Reserved --> Settled: verified usage Reserved --> HeldForReconciliation: timeout or unknown outcome HeldForReconciliation --> Settled: usage recovered HeldForReconciliation --> Released: confirmed no charge Settled --> [*] Released --> [*] Mermaid source Copy Mermaid stateDiagram-v2 [*] --> Reserved: atomic admission Reserved --> Settled: verified usage Reserved --> HeldForReconciliation: timeout or unknown outcome HeldForReconciliation --> Settled: usage recovered HeldForReconciliation --> Released: confirmed no charge Settled --> [*] Released --> [*] A reservation is not an in-memory counter. Implement it with a transactional store or a coordination mechanism that can atomically compare the tenant's available allowance and create the reservation. Concurrent requests must not overspend by observing the same balance. Reservation IDs and request IDs must be unique within the intended scope. A retry of an already completed request should retrieve the persisted result or return its existing status instead of spending again. This module generates a new request ID per execution and does not claim HTTP-level idempotency. Add a durable idempotency coordinator before exposing retryable paid mutations. The adapter may fail after a provider accepted the request. Releasing the entire reservation on every exception allows repeated uncertain requests to bypass spending limits. The safe default is to retain the reservation and enqueue reconciliation. Record expiry and escalation rules so held funds do not remain locked forever. 2.5 Timeouts, cancellation and retries Propagate AbortSignal to the provider transport. A local abort does not prove that the remote provider stopped computation. The deadline implementation races the transport promise so the caller is bounded even if an adapter fails to honor cancellation. Do not retry a model call automatically after an ambiguous timeout. Retrying can duplicate charges and produce two divergent outputs. Explicit retries must pass admission again and honor the request's durable idempotency state. Rate-limit responses may support a delayed retry, but only within a documented attempt and time budget. 2.6 Output safety An adapter returns text and measured usage through a narrow object contract. The core rejects empty answers, oversized UTF-8 responses and malformed usage. A provider's refusal, incomplete generation and tool-call response require explicit adapter handling; they must not be disguised as successful plain-text completion. Render model output as text or sanitized Markdown. Do not place it in an unsanitized innerHTML assignment. Treat generated URLs, shell commands, SQL statements and email recipients as untrusted proposals requiring separate validation and authorization. 3. Production implementation pattern The following TypeScript module has no third-party runtime dependencies. It can be compiled with TypeScript targeting ES2022 and the DOM library. It defines all application contracts and the complete orchestration logic within this chapter's boundary. 3.1 src/lifecycle.ts Copy typescript export type Task = "assistant" | "code_review"; export interface Principal { userId: string; tenantId: string; membershipActive: boolean; permissions: ReadonlySet<string>; } export interface GenerationRequest { task: Task; input: string; maxOutputTokens: number; } export interface ModelPolicy { adapterKey: string; modelId: string; maxOutputTokens: number; } export interface Usage { inputTokens: number; outputTokens: number; } export interface ModelResult { text: string; usage: Usage; } export interface ModelAdapter { generate( policy: ModelPolicy, request: GenerationRequest, signal: AbortSignal ): Promise<ModelResult>; } export interface BudgetLedger { reserve(input: { requestId: string; tenantId: string; policy: ModelPolicy; request: GenerationRequest; }): Promise<{ reservationId: string }>; settle(reservationId: string, usage: Usage): Promise<void>; holdForReconciliation( reservationId: string, requestId: string ): Promise<void>; } export interface AuditEvent { requestId: string; tenantId: string; task: Task; outcome: "completed" | "failed" | "reconciliation_failed"; durationMs: number; } export interface Dependencies { policies: Readonly<Record<Task, ModelPolicy>>; adapters: ReadonlyMap<string, ModelAdapter>; ledger: BudgetLedger; audit(event: AuditEvent): void; now(): number; requestId(): string; timeoutMs: number; maxAnswerBytes: number; } export class LifecycleError extends Error { constructor( public readonly code: string, public readonly httpStatus: number ) { super(code); this.name = "LifecycleError"; } } export function parseRequest(value: unknown): GenerationRequest { if (!value || typeof value !== "object" || Array.isArray(value)) { throw new LifecycleError("invalid_request", 400); } const item = value as Record<string, unknown>; const allowed = new Set(["task", "input", "maxOutputTokens"]); if (Object.keys(item).some((key) => !allowed.has(key))) { throw new LifecycleError("unknown_property", 400); } if (item.task !== "assistant" && item.task !== "code_review") { throw new LifecycleError("unsupported_task", 400); } if ( typeof item.input !== "string" || item.input.trim().length === 0 || new TextEncoder().encode(item.input).byteLength > 16_384 ) { throw new LifecycleError("invalid_input", 400); } if ( typeof item.maxOutputTokens !== "number" || !Number.isSafeInteger(item.maxOutputTokens) || item.maxOutputTokens < 1 || item.maxOutputTokens > 4_096 ) { throw new LifecycleError("invalid_output_limit", 400); } return { task: item.task, input: item.input, maxOutputTokens: item.maxOutputTokens }; } function validateUsage(usage: Usage): void { if ( !usage || !Number.isSafeInteger(usage.inputTokens) || usage.inputTokens < 0 || !Number.isSafeInteger(usage.outputTokens) || usage.outputTokens < 0 ) { throw new LifecycleError("invalid_provider_usage", 502); } } export async function generate( principal: Principal, raw: unknown, deps: Dependencies ): Promise<{ requestId: string; text: string; usage: Usage }> { if ( !principal.userId || !principal.tenantId || !principal.membershipActive || !principal.permissions.has("ai:generate") ) { throw new LifecycleError("forbidden", 403); } const request = parseRequest(raw); const policy = deps.policies[request.task]; if ( !policy || !policy.modelId || request.maxOutputTokens > policy.maxOutputTokens ) { throw new LifecycleError("task_policy_rejected", 400); } const adapter = deps.adapters.get(policy.adapterKey); if (!adapter) { throw new LifecycleError("adapter_unavailable", 503); } if ( !Number.isSafeInteger(deps.timeoutMs) || deps.timeoutMs < 1 || !Number.isSafeInteger(deps.maxAnswerBytes) || deps.maxAnswerBytes < 1 ) { throw new LifecycleError("invalid_runtime_policy", 503); } const requestId = deps.requestId(); const started = deps.now(); const reservation = await deps.ledger.reserve({ requestId, tenantId: principal.tenantId, policy, request }); let timer: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> | undefined; const controller = new AbortController(); const emit = (outcome: AuditEvent["outcome"]): void => { try { deps.audit({ requestId, tenantId: principal.tenantId, task: request.task, outcome, durationMs: Math.max(0, deps.now() - started) }); } catch { // Audit transport health must be monitored independently. // Never expose private provider errors through this path. } }; try { const deadline = new Promise<never>((_, reject) => { timer = setTimeout(() => { controller.abort(); reject(new LifecycleError("provider_timeout", 504)); }, deps.timeoutMs); }); const result = await Promise.race([ adapter.generate(policy, request, controller.signal), deadline ]); validateUsage(result.usage); if ( typeof result.text !== "string" || result.text.trim().length === 0 || new TextEncoder().encode(result.text).byteLength > deps.maxAnswerBytes ) { throw new LifecycleError("invalid_provider_output", 502); } await deps.ledger.settle(reservation.reservationId, result.usage); emit("completed"); return { requestId, text: result.text, usage: result.usage }; } catch (error) { try { await deps.ledger.holdForReconciliation( reservation.reservationId, requestId ); } catch { emit("reconciliation_failed"); } emit("failed"); if (error instanceof LifecycleError) { throw error; } throw new LifecycleError("generation_failed", 502); } finally { if (timer !== undefined) { clearTimeout(timer); } } } 3.2 Contract requirements for dependency implementations The ledger's reserve operation must reject exhausted or suspended tenants before returning a reservation ID. Settle must be idempotent and must not double-charge when the same usage is submitted twice. Hold must not overwrite a previously settled reservation. Because settlement itself can fail after committing, reconciliation must inspect durable state before applying another charge. Ledger operations require their own bounded storage deadlines. The model deadline does not bound a stalled database call. The HTTP host should enforce an overall request deadline and reserve time for reconciliation or dispatch that work durably. An execution context's background callback is not a substitute for a durable queue when losing work would lose billing records. The adapter must enforce its own response-body size limit before parsing, translate provider-specific refusal/incomplete states into typed failures, and validate usage fields. It must not accept a request-provided base URL. API credentials belong in managed secrets and must not appear in policies or audit events. The audit implementation should be nonblocking and feed a monitored transport with a defined loss policy. A deployment requiring fail-closed compliance audit must reject admission when durable audit is unavailable; the reference's best-effort telemetry hook does not satisfy that stronger requirement. 4. Complete executable acceptance test The test uses an in-memory ledger only as a deterministic test double. It is not a production accounting implementation and does not claim distributed atomicity. 4.1 src/lifecycle.test.ts Copy typescript import { generate, LifecycleError, type BudgetLedger, type Dependencies, type ModelAdapter, type Principal, type Usage } from "./lifecycle.js"; function assert(condition: unknown, message: string): asserts condition { if (!condition) throw new Error(message); } async function rejects( operation: () => Promise<unknown>, code: string ): Promise<void> { try { await operation(); } catch (error) { assert(error instanceof LifecycleError, "Expected LifecycleError"); assert(error.code === code, "Unexpected error code"); return; } throw new Error("Expected rejection"); } const states = new Map<string, string>(); let reservations = 0; let adapterCalls = 0; const ledger: BudgetLedger = { async reserve(input) { reservations += 1; states.set(input.requestId, "reserved"); return { reservationId: input.requestId }; }, async settle(id: string, usage: Usage) { assert(usage.outputTokens >= 0, "Invalid usage"); states.set(id, "settled"); }, async holdForReconciliation(id: string) { if (states.get(id) !== "settled") states.set(id, "held"); } }; const adapter: ModelAdapter = { async generate() { adapterCalls += 1; return { text: "Validated response", usage: { inputTokens: 12, outputTokens: 4 } }; } }; let sequence = 0; const deps: Dependencies = { policies: { assistant: { adapterKey: "test", modelId: "deterministic-test-adapter", maxOutputTokens: 1024 }, code_review: { adapterKey: "test", modelId: "deterministic-test-adapter", maxOutputTokens: 1024 } }, adapters: new Map([["test", adapter]]), ledger, audit() {}, now: () => Date.now(), requestId: () => "request-" + (++sequence), timeoutMs: 50, maxAnswerBytes: 4096 }; const principal: Principal = { userId: "test-user", tenantId: "test-tenant", membershipActive: true, permissions: new Set(["ai:generate"]) }; const input = { task: "assistant", input: "Explain a transactional outbox.", maxOutputTokens: 128 }; const result = await generate(principal, input, deps); assert(result.text === "Validated response", "Wrong response"); assert(states.get(result.requestId) === "settled", "Not settled"); const beforeDenied = reservations; await rejects( () => generate({ ...principal, membershipActive: false }, input, deps), "forbidden" ); assert(reservations === beforeDenied, "Denied request reserved budget"); await rejects( () => generate(principal, { ...input, model: "client-choice" }, deps), "unknown_property" ); const failing: ModelAdapter = { async generate() { throw new Error("Sensitive upstream detail"); } }; await rejects( () => generate(principal, input, { ...deps, adapters: new Map([["test", failing]]) }), "generation_failed" ); assert(states.get("request-" + sequence) === "held", "Failure not held"); const stalled: ModelAdapter = { async generate() { return new Promise(() => {}); } }; await rejects( () => generate(principal, input, { ...deps, timeoutMs: 5, adapters: new Map([["test", stalled]]) }), "provider_timeout" ); assert(states.get("request-" + sequence) === "held", "Timeout not held"); assert(adapterCalls === 1, "Unexpected successful adapter calls"); console.log("Lifecycle acceptance tests passed"); 4.2 Compiler configuration Save this complete configuration as tsconfig.json. Install TypeScript as a development dependency, commit the generated package lock, and use the same locked compiler in CI. Copy json { "compilerOptions": { "target": "ES2022", "module": "NodeNext", "moduleResolution": "NodeNext", "lib": ["ES2022", "DOM"], "strict": true, "outDir": "dist", "rootDir": "src", "skipLibCheck": true, "noEmitOnError": true }, "include": ["src/**/*.ts"] } Set the package's type field to module so the test's top-level await uses ECMAScript modules. Run the compiler followed by the emitted test: Copy sh npm pkg set type=module npm install --save-dev typescript npx tsc --project tsconfig.json node dist/lifecycle.test.js Do not substitute synthetic model IDs into a live provider. The deterministic-test-adapter string is a real test fixture identifier consumed only by the test double. 5. Deployment configuration and secret boundaries This chapter's module does not start a public HTTP listener. Integrate it behind the application's authenticated gateway, then bind concrete ledger and provider adapters. Publishing a raw unauthenticated wrapper would violate the invariants in Section 1. For a Cloudflare deployment, keep the compatibility date explicit and use version-controlled non-secret configuration. Provision provider credentials as Worker secrets or approved Secret Store bindings. Verify each environment separately because resource and secret binding behavior must not be assumed to inherit across environments. The following is an application policy document, not a Wrangler manifest. An admission configuration loader must validate every property and reject unknown keys. Copy yaml version: 1 request_policy: maximum_body_bytes: 24576 maximum_input_utf8_bytes: 16384 maximum_output_tokens: 4096 maximum_answer_utf8_bytes: 65536 model_deadline_ms: 25000 require_active_membership: true required_permission: ai:generate automatic_provider_retries: 0 accounting_policy: reserve_before_inference: true unknown_outcome: hold_for_reconciliation settlement_idempotency: required logging_policy: include_request_id: true include_tenant_id: true include_duration: true include_prompt: false include_generated_text: false include_credentials: false The limits are deliberately local policy values, not provider quotas. The gateway body limit is larger than the input-string limit to allow JSON syntax and metadata while bounding memory use. The output byte ceiling is independent of output-token limits. A generated Unicode answer can consume more bytes than its visible length suggests. A Docker image is not needed for the Workers runtime. Container deployment is a separate target requiring its own HTTP server, signal handling, health checks and secret injection. Including a nonfunctional Dockerfile would make this chapter less complete, not more deployable. 6. Acceptance, testing and verification matrix Area Concrete test Required result Identity Expired session reaches gateway 401 before lifecycle invocation; no reservation or model call Authorization Inactive membership or missing permission 403; no provider activity Tenant isolation Client changes tenant header or object ID Membership check rejects unauthorized tenant Input schema Unknown property, blank input, array body, unsupported task 400 before reservation Unicode Input exceeds 16,384 UTF-8 bytes with multibyte characters Rejected using encoded byte length Token policy Output ceiling exceeds registry maximum Rejected before inference Registry Adapter missing or model unapproved Fail closed; no user-controlled fallback Budget concurrency Parallel requests compete for final allowance Durable ledger admits only affordable reservations Successful completion Adapter returns valid text and usage Exactly one idempotent settlement and safe response Provider transport Connection resets after request submission Reservation retained for reconciliation Timeout Adapter ignores AbortSignal Caller still receives bounded timeout Output Empty text, oversized bytes or invalid usage 502; uncertain spend remains reserved Settlement uncertainty Database commits then connection fails Reconciliation reads existing state; no duplicate charge Telemetry Audit destination fails Alert under defined loss policy; no credential leakage Rendering Model emits script, HTML or executable command Displayed as inert data; no automatic execution Retry Client resubmits a paid request Durable idempotency coordinator applies documented replay policy Recovery Held reservation exceeds reconciliation objective Alert and audited investigation; no silent release Secrets Inspect static assets and logs No provider keys, OTPs, bearer tokens or private prompts Rollback Registry version regresses quality Restore approved version without weakening authorization 6.1 Operational objectives Define service objectives before launch: admission availability, successful-request latency, timeout rate, unresolved-reservation age and cost per accepted task. Set thresholds from measured staging traffic and the business risk profile. The chapter does not invent universal production percentages. Alert on oldest unresolved reservation, repeated settlement errors, provider authorization failures and unexpected token growth. A model outage should degrade the AI feature while preserving identity, accounting records and ordinary application access. 6.2 Known implementation traps An in-memory limiter is instance-local and cannot enforce a global tenant allowance. A provider API key scoped to a whole organization can exceed the authority needed by one application. A fallback model with different retention terms can violate a data-processing policy even when its output is correct. A provider response marked incomplete may include text that must not be accepted as a finished result. Setting a provider's store flag to false does not by itself establish contractual zero-data-retention coverage. 7. Official provider and standards references - OpenAI model catalog : current model families and capability discovery. - OpenAI Responses create reference : provider request and response semantics. - Claude model overview : model IDs, capabilities and lifecycle. - Gemini model catalog : model endpoints and modality-specific choices. - Cloudflare Worker configuration : deployment configuration. - Cloudflare Worker secrets : runtime credential handling. - OWASP Authentication Cheat Sheet : identity control boundaries. - OWASP Authorization Cheat Sheet : permission checks and least privilege. - Mermaid documentation : editable diagram syntax and rendering. 8. Chapter completion and next page Page 1 defines the lifecycle, trust boundaries, complete orchestration module, deterministic tests, policy configuration and deployment acceptance requirements. It does not assert that a public service has been provisioned or approved. The next standalone chapter is Page 2 — Identity, Authentication, SSO, Sessions and Tenant Authorization . It will define the concrete gateway boundary used by this lifecycle. Ready to proceed to Page 2. Process and decision gates Validate the authenticated principal, active tenant membership and operation permission. Validate the request schema and select an approved adapter from the server registry. Reserve the tenant's budget atomically before provider invocation. Invoke the adapter with a bounded deadline; treat cancellation as an uncertain remote outcome. Validate output and usage, settle accounting idempotently, or retain the reservation for reconciliation. Related apps, software and third parties Component Responsibility and boundary GitHub and GitHub Actions Versioned code, documentation review and reproducible acceptance checks. CI success must be tied to the tested revision. Cloudflare Workers Possible authenticated request host. Bind concrete identity, ledger and provider transports; the chapter module does not expose a public endpoint. Transactional database or coordinated ledger Atomic budget reservation and idempotent settlement. An instance-local counter cannot enforce a distributed tenant balance. OpenAI, Claude or Gemini adapter Approved model transport selected by exact capability and data policy. Provider credentials remain server-side. OpenTelemetry Redacted correlation and operational signals. Exclude prompts, generated private content and credentials from routine telemetry. Ownership, maintenance and related knowledge The platform owner approves registry and accounting policy changes. The on-call owner investigates held reservations and provider transport failures. Re-run the acceptance matrix after changing model contracts, authentication, database isolation or timeout behavior. Preserve the last approved registry version and reconcile unresolved reservations before retiring a deployment. Authentication · Model routing · Operations and recovery 6. Implementation Pattern and Copyable Code This focused TypeScript implementation belongs in the trusted application or test layer. Supply identity, permission and provider-verification state from real verified dependencies; do not accept trust flags directly from a browser. typescript Copy code type Capability = "text" | "vision" | "json"; interface Candidate { id: string; approved: boolean; capabilities: ReadonlySet<Capability>; privateDataAllowed: boolean; } export function compatibleCandidates( candidates: readonly Candidate[], required: readonly Capability[], includesPrivateData: boolean ): Candidate[] { return candidates.filter(candidate => candidate.approved && (!includesPrivateData || candidate.privateDataAllowed) && required.every(capability => candidate.capabilities.has(capability)) ); } Version the implementation with the consuming application and run this chapter’s acceptance checks when its assumptions change. A copied unit does not establish that all external integrations are active. 7. Mermaid Architecture and Process Diagram Production AI Application Architecture — decision process flowchart TD A["Validate task contract and capability requirements"] --> B["Reserve budget and invoke approved adapter"] B --> C{"Acceptance and policy pass"} C -->|Yes| D["Validate output and settle or reconcile usage"] C -->|No| E["Stop and investigate"] Mermaid source mermaid Copy code flowchart TD A["Validate task contract and capability requirements"] --> B["Reserve budget and invoke approved adapter"] B --> C{"Acceptance and policy pass"} C -->|Yes| D["Validate output and settle or reconcile usage"] C -->|No| E["Stop and investigate"] 8. Failure Modes, Edge Cases and Security Failure Containment Fallback weakens data policy Stop the affected operation; inspect its last durable boundary and redacted evidence. Reconcile uncertain side effects before retrying and add a regression case. Timeout releases budget despite uncertain charge Stop the affected operation; inspect its last durable boundary and redacted evidence. Reconcile uncertain side effects before retrying and add a regression case. Authorize tenant-owned inputs and artifacts explicitly. Distinguish permanent validation failures from transient dependency errors. Exclude raw session tokens, credentials, OTPs and private content from routine logs. 9. Acceptance, Testing and Verification Matrix Case Expected outcome Evidence No model call before reservation Condition holds in the intended environment; failure blocks approval. Tested revision, input, observed result and reviewer Unknown outcome holds funds for reconciliation Condition holds in the intended environment; failure blocks approval. Tested revision, input, observed result and reviewer Priority negative paths Fallback weakens data policy; Timeout releases budget despite uncertain charge Reproduction and containment Standalone HTML Complete chapter is readable before JavaScript executes Inspect source and disable JavaScript Copy and Mermaid Exact source remains available without diagram preview Copy/paste and module-load failure checks 10. Operations, Ownership and Maintenance Assign a technical owner for model routing & evaluation. Review changes to Model registry, Budget ledger, Model adapter against this chapter’s assumptions. Record the dependency contract, environment and last tested revision. Use the failure matrix to locate uncertain state during incidents. Preserve redacted evidence, restore the approved configuration or apply a reviewed correction, and rerun acceptance checks. Update the review date after provider or architectural changes. 11. chapters.title: Databases & Storage
chapters.text: CHAPTER 09 · ENGINEERING KNOWLEDGE Databases & Storage Version Reviewed Architecture scope 2.0.0 2 November 2026 Protect integrity, tenant isolation and recoverability across storage layers. 1. Description, Purpose and Boundaries Protect integrity, tenant isolation and recoverability across storage layers. Choose storage by consistency, query patterns, tenancy and recovery requirements. Start with the data lifecycle before selecting a product. Treat databases & storage as an independently reviewable capability. Trace its inputs, processing decisions and acceptance evidence before applying it to a live system. The examples define bounded units; external services need separately verified permissions, contracts and environment configuration. 2. Architectural Principles and Decisions The primary decision boundary is: Apply constrained schema and versioned migrations. Application logic and an accountable owner establish this decision. Preserve the input identity and rule revision so its outcome can be investigated. Prioritize cross-tenant queries omit membership filter and migration locks or rewrites large tables. Establish checks for these failures before enabling automation. Completion requires evidence for the final step, verify tenant isolation and restore backups, rather than merely observing request acceptance. 3. Process, Inputs and Outputs Step Action Evidence 1 Define entities, relationships and access patterns Approved input scope, source and owner 2 Apply constrained schema and versioned migrations Recorded decision, revision and exception handling 3 Verify tenant isolation and restore backups Observed outcome and recovery or rollback decision Stop at any boundary whose required evidence cannot be established. If an external side effect may already have occurred, reconcile its durable identity before retrying. 4. Related Apps, Software and Third Parties Component Role Integration responsibility D1 SQLite-based managed SQL Verify supported contract, least privilege, account access, data handling, quotas and ownership. PostgreSQL Relational database Verify supported contract, least privilege, account access, data handling, quotas and ownership. R2 Object storage Verify supported contract, least privilege, account access, data handling, quotas and ownership. These products are candidates for this capability, not a claim that they are connected to this documentation site. Choose them by boundary responsibility and measured requirements. Keep their private credentials outside public HTML. 5. Detailed Mechanics and Topic Features Storage types Relational databases suit structured records, joins, constraints and transactions. Document stores suit evolving aggregate documents. Key-value stores suit simple lookups and caches. Object storage holds files and exports. Vector indexes support similarity retrieval; retain authoritative records separately. Search indexes support text discovery. Time-series and analytical stores support event analysis. A cache or search index should not silently become the only copy of critical data. Cloudflare reference mapping D1 provides SQL storage for Workers applications; R2 holds objects; KV supports distributed key-value access; Durable Objects can coordinate state and concurrency. Evaluate each service’s current consistency and transaction semantics before choosing it for sessions, OTP counters or locks. Keep development, demo, staging and production resource identifiers separate. Bind resources to the backend; never place database credentials in public HTML. Schema and integrity Model users, identities, memberships, roles, sessions, auth_challenges, email_outbox, delivery_events and audit_events. Include tenant_id where applicable, creation and expiry timestamps, unique identity constraints, foreign keys and indexes matching real queries. Authorize tenant access server-side on every operation. Use parameterized queries. Define deletion, retention and export rules before collecting sensitive data. Implementation and verification Document access patterns → select store → define schema and constraints → apply versioned migrations → provision least-privilege bindings → implement repository/query layer → test isolation and concurrent writes → rehearse restore. Use additive migrations before destructive changes. A backup is useful only after a restore test; define recovery-point and recovery-time objectives. Measure query plans and latency before adding indexes or caches. 6. Implementation Pattern and Copyable Code Use these schema constraints or conditional statements through the target database’s parameter-binding API. Confirm transaction and concurrency semantics before deployment. sql Copy code PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON; CREATE TABLE tenants ( id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT NOT NULL ); CREATE TABLE documents ( id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, tenant_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES tenants(id), title TEXT NOT NULL, body TEXT NOT NULL, version INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1 CHECK (version > 0), created_at INTEGER NOT NULL ); CREATE INDEX documents_tenant_created ON documents(tenant_id, created_at); -- Bind both values with the database driver's prepared-statement API. SELECT id, title, version FROM documents WHERE tenant_id = ? AND id = ?; Version the implementation with the consuming application and run this chapter’s acceptance checks when its assumptions change. A copied unit does not establish that all external integrations are active. 7. Mermaid Architecture and Process Diagram Databases & Storage — decision process flowchart TD A["Define entities, relationships and access patterns"] --> B["Apply constrained schema and versioned migrations"] B --> C{"Acceptance and policy pass"} C -->|Yes| D["Verify tenant isolation and restore backups"] C -->|No| E["Stop and investigate"] Mermaid source mermaid Copy code flowchart TD A["Define entities, relationships and access patterns"] --> B["Apply constrained schema and versioned migrations"] B --> C{"Acceptance and policy pass"} C -->|Yes| D["Verify tenant isolation and restore backups"] C -->|No| E["Stop and investigate"] 8. Failure Modes, Edge Cases and Security Failure Containment Cross-tenant queries omit membership filter Stop the affected operation; inspect its last durable boundary and redacted evidence. Reconcile uncertain side effects before retrying and add a regression case. Migration locks or rewrites large tables Stop the affected operation; inspect its last durable boundary and redacted evidence. Reconcile uncertain side effects before retrying and add a regression case. Authorize tenant-owned inputs and artifacts explicitly. Distinguish permanent validation failures from transient dependency errors. Exclude raw session tokens, credentials, OTPs and private content from routine logs. 9. Acceptance, Testing and Verification Matrix Case Expected outcome Evidence Duplicate identities rejected by constraints Condition holds in the intended environment; failure blocks approval. Tested revision, input, observed result and reviewer Restore recovers documented recovery point Condition holds in the intended environment; failure blocks approval. Tested revision, input, observed result and reviewer Priority negative paths Cross-tenant queries omit membership filter; Migration locks or rewrites large tables Reproduction and containment Standalone HTML Complete chapter is readable before JavaScript executes Inspect source and disable JavaScript Copy and Mermaid Exact source remains available without diagram preview Copy/paste and module-load failure checks 10. Verify the sender identity, account production-access status and current sending quotas in the same region. Never embed SMTP credentials in browser code or publish them in the knowledge center. Domain authentication Configure DKIM using the provider-issued records. Set SPF for the actual envelope sender; do not create multiple SPF records at one name. Publish DMARC with a monitored rollout and verify alignment. If using a custom MAIL FROM domain, use its exact region-specific MX/SPF instructions. Distinguish visible From, Reply-To, envelope MAIL FROM and return-path roles. DNS examples must not replace provider-issued values. Detailed Mechanics and Topic Features Challenge lifecycle POST /auth/otp/request validates input, abuse limits and the server-verified challenge. Generate codes with a cryptographic random generator. Return an opaque challenge identifier and a generic acknowledgement. Bind the stored challenge to identity, purpose and expiry. For short numeric codes, store a keyed HMAC verifier with a separately protected server key; an ordinary hash alone is easy to enumerate offline. Never log or return the code. Example policy and data Example: an eight-digit code, five-minute lifetime, five verification attempts and a 60-second resend cooldown. Tune limits to risk and usability and apply aggregate limits by account and network. Store id, user or normalized identity reference, purpose, verifier, expires_at, attempts, consumed_at and generation. Make resend behavior explicit: invalidate the previous generation and clearly tell users only the newest code works. Atomic verification POST /auth/otp/verify checks expiry, purpose, generation and attempt budget server-side. Atomically compare/consume the challenge or use a transaction/conditional update so two concurrent submissions cannot both succeed. Increment failed-attempt counters atomically. On success rotate/create the session, mark identity verification only for the correct purpose and reject replay. A reset code must not authorize an unrelated sensitive action. Abuse and delivery failures Use generic responses and reasonably consistent timing to reduce account enumeration. Do not lock an account merely because someone requested codes. Apply request and verify throttles separately. Queue failures must not produce unlimited valid challenges. Expired email jobs should be dropped rather than delivering unusable codes. Avoid relying on email-link GET requests to consume credentials because mail scanners may prefetch links. Test matrix Cover valid, incorrect, expired, reused, superseded and wrong-purpose codes; simultaneous verification; resend floods; exhausted attempts; delayed email; SMTP outage; forged Turnstile token; and account enumeration. Turnstile tokens require Siteverify validation, are single use and expire after 300 seconds. Validate expected hostname and action where used; a widget alone does not protect the endpoint. 6. Detailed Mechanics and Topic Features Session design Generate high-entropy opaque session tokens; store a digest or keyed verifier server-side with user, tenant, assurance level, issued_at, last_seen_at and expires_at. Use Secure, HttpOnly cookies with an appropriate SameSite policy and narrow scope. Rotate identifiers after login and privilege changes. Enforce idle and absolute timeouts on the server. Logout must revoke server-side state. Access-control models RBAC assigns permissions through roles; ABAC evaluates attributes such as tenant or resource ownership; relationship-based rules model shared access. Default deny. Verify permissions for every API request, object read, download and mutation. Hiding an admin button is not authorization. Do not accept roles or tenant identifiers from the browser without validating them against session membership. Browser and API boundaries Use CSRF protection for cookie-authenticated state changes, validate Origin where appropriate and restrict CORS to intended origins. CORS is not an authentication layer. Keep long-lived bearer tokens out of browser-accessible storage when a secure cookie session fits the architecture. Validate JWT signatures and claims; plan key rotation and revocation rather than merely decoding tokens. Acceptance checks Test cross-tenant object IDs, revoked sessions, expired cookies, role downgrade, logout on another device, CSRF attempts, forged JWTs and direct privileged endpoints. Log decisions with correlation IDs while excluding raw tokens. Reauthenticate before sensitive exports, payment changes and factor enrollment. 6.
